extracted.intended_audience: Principal Investigators and senior/key personnel preparing NIH-style grant applications and biosketches
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and content examples for completing Senior/Key Person Profiles, biographical sketches, and the 'Other Facilities/Equipment' sections of an NIH-style grant application. Includes required fields, section headings, page limits, and examples of acceptable content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors in the order listed on Form Page 2. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FOUR PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include name, eRA Commons user name (credential), position title, education/training table, and the standardized sections (Personal Statement; Positions and Honors; Other Experience and Professional Memberships; Selected Peer-reviewed Publications; Research Support). Strictly adhere to the four-page maximum per person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Statement content
rubrics_metrics.description: A. Personal Statement — describe the goal of the proposed research, your role on the project, and your relevant experience and expertise as it relates to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain specific responsibilities (e.g., oversee experiments, reporting, administrative/financial duties, interface with other investigators), prior relevant work and collaborative relationships, and salient translational accomplishments (e.g., patents, bench-to-bedside progress). Use the Personal Statement to justify the individual's fit and capability for the proposed role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education/Training entry
rubrics_metrics.description: EDUCATION/TRAINING (Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, include postdoctoral training and residency training if applicable.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide institution and location, degree (if applicable), month/year, and field of study for each training entry in chronological order beginning with the baccalaureate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positions and Employment (Positions and Honors)
rubrics_metrics.description: List Positions and Employment in chronological order, including titles, departments, institutions, and years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include notable administrative roles (e.g., Chair, Director), academic appointments with dates, and honors or awards. Use this section to show career progression and leadership experience relevant to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Experience and Professional Memberships
rubrics_metrics.description: Document other experience and professional memberships, including service on review panels, advisory committees, and editorial or professional society roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List NIH study section service, committee memberships, and other professional activities that demonstrate peer-review experience and domain leadership; include dates and appointing organizations where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selected Peer-reviewed Publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a selection of peer-reviewed publications relevant to the individual's expertise and the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select representative publications (the example shows selecting from a larger corpus), include full citation details, and where relevant include PMCID/PMID. Focus on works that support the individual's qualifications for the proposed role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Support (Ongoing and Completed)
rubrics_metrics.description: List ongoing and completed research support including grant numbers, PI(s), dates, project titles/major goals, and the individual's role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate ongoing and completed support. For each entry include funding mechanism, project period, brief major goal, and explicit role (e.g., PI, Co-Investigator, Biostatistician). This documents capacity, potential overlap, and relevant experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required attachments for Senior/Key Person Profile
rubrics_metrics.description: RESEARCH & RELATED Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) *Attach Biographical SketchAttach Current & Pending Support
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach both the biographical sketch and a Current & Pending Support document for each senior/key person as part of the expanded profile submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the order listed on Form Page 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the requested information for Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors in the order listed on Form Page 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain the ordering specified by the form when preparing profiles and attachments to ensure consistency with the form page and administrative review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profile form field completeness (Project Role and credentials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Profile entries must include fields such as Prefix, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Organization Name, Division, Position/Title, Department, Street, Phone Number, E-Mail, Credential (e.g., agency login), Project Role, Other Project Role Category, Degree Type, Degree Year, and Country/State/Zip as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all required form fields (marked with *) and ensure Project Role and Other Project Role Category accurately reflect the individual's involvement (e.g., PD/PI, Co-Investigator, Consultant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Facilities — describe resources and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Other Facilities High performance computing (HPC): describe resources (CPU, storage, software tools, etc.) and assistance (training, operational support, software development) necessary to fully utilize high-performance computation in research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide cluster specifications (e.g., compute nodes, CPU cores, RAM, storage), available compilers and libraries, domain-specific applications (R, MATLAB), and description of support staff and services (technical assistance, training, application porting/tuning). Document institutional partnerships (e.g., with IBM) and major shared assets (e.g., BlueHive, BlueGene) where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Facilities — describe core facilities and instrumentation
rubrics_metrics.description: For cores and centralized resources (e.g., sequencing, imaging, proteomics, vivarium), describe services provided, instrumentation available, and expertise offered to investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List specific instruments (model names where possible), services (DNA/RNA extraction, sequencing platforms, flow cytometry, mass spectrometry, imaging modalities), library collections (chemical compound libraries), and any training, standardization, or validation support the core provides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivarium compliance and accreditation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Vivarium is a centralized resource facility... These facilities are fully accredited by AAALAC and are in compliance with state law, federal statute and NIH policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State accreditation status (e.g., AAALAC), staffing qualifications (board-certified veterinarian, trained technicians), and compliance with applicable laws and NIH policies in the vivarium description to demonstrate regulatory readiness and animal care oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core/Facility capability statements for grant support
rubrics_metrics.description: Cores should document capacity to develop assays, screen libraries, provide preliminary data for grant proposals, and support larger screening efforts to identify leads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include capability to develop and validate assays, list robotic/liquid handling instruments, plate readers, types and sizes of chemical libraries available, and examples of use cases (preliminary data generation, lead identification, assay development for proposals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide concrete instrumentation and equipment listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Major equipment available for the project should be enumerated (e.g., biosafety cabinets, thermocyclers, spectrophotometers, centrifuges, flow cytometers, real-time PCR instruments, freezers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts, models, and locations where possible, and distinguish between personal/lab equipment and department/core instrumentation available via recharge.
